title: Once Upon a Time...

beats.what: The boy in white appears in recap; the full nursery rhyme is assembled and Elgin identifies it as an old rhyme
Julie convulses and is placed in a bed at Colony House; she is catatonic and getting cold
Silver bullets brought from the RV are confirmed useless: Randall was not dead despite a direct shot
Boyd and Kenny bring Sara to the clearing where Boyd's worm infection began; Sara hears the music box
Sara receives what the music box is communicating: it needs three people to die; the creatures are its instruments
Boyd prays Psalm 23 over Sara in the clearing; this appears to interrupt the music box's hold on her
Tabitha tells Jim she must go to the tower and asks his permission to leave; she invokes Victor's mother
Victor takes Tabitha to the bottle tree; reveals his mother's body was found here, outside the tree, on the night everyone died
Tabitha enters the bottle tree alone, disappearing from the town
Ellis and Fatima get married in a hillside ceremony officiated by Boyd
Boyd descends into the tunnels alone to find the music box's source
Boyd smashes the music box; Julie and Marielle revive; the buzzing stops
A creature attacks Boyd in the tunnel; Sara intervenes and sacrifices herself so Boyd can escape
Boyd surfaces from the tunnels; Ethan asks where his mother is; Jim has no answer
Season finale kicker: a woman wakes in St. Anthony's Hospital, three days after hikers found her unconscious in the woods

character_beats.beat: Wants to be worthy of the hero role the town assigned him; an imagined dead Tom tells him he has been looking at the symbol wrong, and that only the tunnels hold the answer; Boyd descends alone
Wants to save Julie and believes the tower is the only path; asks Jim's blessing not because she needs it but because she needs him to let her go, knowing Victor's mother never came back
Spends the hour trying to earn her place in the town through usefulness; ends it by choosing to die so Boyd can live, completing the arc from murderer to self-sacrifice

key_lines.line: It's not your fear that feeds the forest, Boyd.
key_lines.why: Reverses the season's established logic; hope, not fear, is the engine of suffering here

key_lines.line: Just because we're only a thread doesn't mean we don't matter.
key_lines.why: Boyd reframes collective sacrifice; seeds the possibility trapped people are preconditions for others' escape
Sara translates the music box: Boyd's act of heroism in E06 was the direct cause of the finale crisis
Recurs 15 times in the episode clustered in the tunnel sequence; the most-repeated unit is a word nobody in the town can translate

open_loops: Where does Tabitha emerge from the bottle tree and what is the tower she is looking for?
The woman waking in St. Anthony's Hospital: who is she and how did she get out of the town?
The boy in white told Elgin the rhyme and appeared to Boyd's group: what is he?
Victor grew up in the town alone after everyone died; what does his unbroken survival mean about the town's rules?
With the music box destroyed, can the creatures still kill, or was it the box that directed them?
Khatri appears to Boyd in the tunnels: is this the same mechanism as Boyd's earlier Khatri visions or something the town is generating?

payoffs.plants_from: S02E08 44:40 (Victor's mother went toward the tower and never returned)
payoffs.what: Victor finds his mother's body at the bottle tree: she did not make it inside; Tabitha chooses to attempt what Eloise failed

payoffs.plants_from: S02E06 35:24 (Boyd brings worm infection back to town)
payoffs.what: Sara confirms the music box is laughing because Boyd brought the entity back; the heroic act of E06 is retrospectively a catastrophic error

payoffs.plants_from: S02E09 44:45 (boy in white delivers nursery rhyme)
payoffs.what: The boy in white is identified across multiple dreamers as a single source; the rhyme's three-victim structure is now the mechanism being acted out on Julie, Marielle, and Randall

payoffs.plants_from: S02E07 35:53 (bile extracted as weapon) and S02E09 24:23 (silver bullets prepared)
payoffs.what: Silver bullets failed: Randall is alive. The bile weapon, pinned as the season's big discovery, does not work as a field weapon at distance

contradiction.wants: to keep everyone safe and bear the cost of leadership himself
contradiction.does: descends alone into the tunnels without telling anyone what he knows, making himself the single point of failure for the entire town's survival

tone_notes: At 58 minutes this is the longest episode in the run; words per minute drops to 69.6, the lowest of any episode here. The top silence at 05:58-07:54 (116 seconds) falls between the silver bullet failure and the Sara-in-the-clearing scene, giving the loss of the weapon its full weight. Minutes 8-10 spike to 171 w/min for the Sara music box scene, then density collapses for the ceremony (minutes 41-47 average 40-66 w/min), letting the wedding breathe against the ongoing crisis. The phrase 'anghkooey' appears 15 times, clustered in minutes 37-38 as Boyd enters the tunnel, functioning as the episode's sonic texture rather than dialogue. The final scene outside the town carries zero ambient density; the hospital cut lands in silence.
